leading_positions.synthesis: Both supporters propose Crews, Deshaies and Handa for targeted protein degradation, combining the PROTAC concept with the cereblon mechanism of molecular glues. They share the view that induced proximity is a transferable mechanistic principle and that the field is reproduced across laboratories and E3 ligases. Their citation wording differs slightly: one stresses the bifunctional PROTAC and cereblon-dependent glue mechanism, the other adds thalidomide-type drug action. Both concede that Ciulli (VHL ligands, ternary-complex structure) has a claim that goes unrecognised, that Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are also credited in the field, and that no approved degrader drug exists yet.

Both supporters propose Liu, Komor and Gaudelli for base editing, with the citation centred on programmable chemical conversion of a single DNA base without double-strand cleavage. Both name the same costs: proximity to the 2020 CRISPR-Cas9 prize, the independent parallel Target-AID work of Kondo and Nishida, and a clinical record that is still young. They differ in emphasis: one stresses the directed evolution of an adenine deaminase and relevance to genome maintenance and repair, the other stresses a clear principle and separating the 2016-2017 discovery from later refinements such as prime editing. The chair is a supporter of this position and the summary should be read with that in mind.

Both supporters propose Buchwald and Hartwig for general palladium-catalysed C-N cross-coupling, citing a clean two-name attribution, roughly thirty years of use and no maturity question. Both name the same objections: the 2010 cross-coupling prize may already cover the paradigm, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling complicates priority. Both state that they are recalling the Kosugi history from memory, so its weight is unresolved in the files. This is the only leading position whose case rests on a synthetic method rather than a biological capability.

A single member proposes Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen for biomolecular phase separation as a physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation. The proposer acknowledges thin support, disputed physiological relevance of condensates, an unsettled third name (Rosen versus Pappu and Mittag), and a possible Physiology or Medicine framing.

A single member proposes Corma, Davis and Zones for the design of zeolite and molecular-sieve catalysts. The proposer states that no colleague ranked it in the opening round, that early pioneers (Barrer, Milton, Breck) fall outside the credited names, and that Yu and Tsapatsis are excluded by the three-name limit.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members propose a single-part prize in round 1, and no member proposes a split or multi-part configuration.

Every member names the same shortlist-internal competitors as alternatives or reservations: B012, B060 and B055 recur across the statements, and B019 is raised by two members as the safest translational choice.

Members agree that the three-laureate limit cannot cover the PROTAC and molecular-glue field without leaving out a real contribution, and that this applies to base editing (Target-AID) and phase separation as well.

Every statement identifies the strongest case against its own preferred candidate, and in each case that case concerns attribution, overlap with an earlier prize, or maturity rather than the underlying science being in doubt.
No member reports a personal or institutional conflict with any credited name; scientific proximity is disclosed instead.
scientific_disputes: Whether C-N cross-coupling (B055) is a conceptually new achievement or an extension of the Pd(0)/Pd(II) manifold recognised in 2010; B012 supporters question its novelty, B055 supporters question whether PROTAC work is mainly medicinal-chemistry design rather than new chemistry.
Whether base editing (B060) is distinct from CRISPR-Cas9 or an application layer on an already recognised nuclease.
Whether PROTACs and cereblon-dependent molecular glues are one mechanistic achievement or two separate lineages that should not share a citation.
Whether condensates (B061) are functionally essential in vivo or partly artefacts of concentration, overexpression or crowding.
Whether the zeolite field (B018) is a single discovery or diffuse industrial refinement.
attribution_disputes: B012: the third seat for the Crews and Deshaies pair is contested between Handa (cereblon identification) and Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex structure); Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito are also credited. Both B012 proposers chose Handa, so Ciulli is left out of every configuration in this round.
B060: Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) reported a cytidine-deaminase fusion essentially in parallel with the Liu laboratory; both B060 proposers use a Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio that omits them.
B055: Kosugi's tin-amide coupling is a precursor, and a Buchwald and Hartwig pair deliberately omits him; two members cite memory, not verified literature, for this history.
B061: the third name is open between Rosen and the Pappu and Mittag pair.
B018: foundational zeolite figures lie outside the credited names, and Yu and Tsapatsis are excluded by the three-name limit.

Apparently similar proposals differ in laureates: B012 as proposed pairs Crews and Deshaies with Handa, whereas statements from others discuss Ciulli as an alternative third name, and the two B012 citations differ in whether the mechanism is cereblon-specific.
maturity_disputes: B012: no approved degrader drug yet exists, so members disagree whether this is disqualifying or only a timing risk.
B060: clinical use has begun but long-term in vivo safety, bystander edits and off-target deamination are not settled.
B061: roughly fifteen years of confirmation, but physiological relevance is still under test.
B055 and B018 are described by their supporters as mature, with no timing concern; the disputes there concern novelty and attribution.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Zou Xiaodong: B018 (zeolites and porous frameworks) lies in her own research field and she knows the community professionally, including Jihong Yu; no collaboration or institutional tie is recorded, and she says she would step back if a closer tie were shown.
Sparr Emma: B019 overlaps directly with her lipid self-assembly work and B061 touches her soft-matter field; she flags scientific proximity only.
Aili Daniel: research overlap with Sparr in peptide and lipid self-assembly and nanoparticle biosensing, related to B019 and B061; flagged for the committee to judge, no specific conflict.
Chabes Andrei: his work on dNTP pools and replication fidelity is in the same broad area of genome maintenance as base editing (B060); no tie to any credited candidate.

Brzezinski Peter: serves as Secretary and deputy Nobel Foundation board member, which he describes as procedural, and notes a Stockholm University colleague relationship with Zou; no conflict with a shortlisted candidate.
Linke Heiner (chair): supports B060 and discloses no connection to the Liu, Komor or Gaudelli laboratories.
questions_for_round2: B012 supporters: if the third seat must be chosen, is the committee prepared to credit Handa (cereblon and glues) over Ciulli (VHL ligands and ternary-complex design), and does the citation then describe one achievement or two?

B060 supporters: what distinguishes base editing from CRISPR-Cas9 in a form that can be stated in one citation sentence, and does the committee accept excluding Kondo and Nishida, or is a fourth name required?

B055 supporters: can the committee state what C-N coupling added conceptually beyond the 2010 prize, and how far did Kosugi's work anticipate the ligand-controlled catalytic cycle, with the evidence for that history placed on the record?
Is a molecule-making prize (B055), a chemical-biology or tools prize (B012, B060), or another category the committee's priority this year, and does any member move to a two-part configuration?

For B061 and B018, which are each supported by one member only, what would the proposers need to see for the committee to treat them as competitive, and can the B061 physiological-relevance concern be resolved?
Does the absence of an approved degrader drug and the youth of the base-editing clinical record weigh differently, and should maturity be judged by independent confirmation or by clinical outcome?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows three two-member blocs (B012, B060, B055) and two single-member positions (B061, B018), so no configuration has the five-vote majority. The leading candidates differ in kind: a chemical-biology mechanism with an unresolved third name, a tool with an overlap and attribution question, and a mature synthetic method with a novelty question. Each member has stated the main weakness of the candidate they prefer. The chair belongs to one of the two-member blocs and has tried to describe all positions in the same terms.
